description:
Problem: local.exclusive (local.py:293-315) takes one flock on ~/.cache/benchbox/local-oracle/review.lock for every make pr-open review on the machine; a second review waits up to an hour, so one slow review blocks every other agent's PR (2026-10-27: an urgent fix waited behind another session's review). No recorded reason exists for a machine-wide scope.

First-principles analysis (2026-10-27, from code): each review's state is private: a mkdtemp work directory holding plan, homes, workspace clone and attempts (local.py:643-648); process survivor checks are scoped to the review's own process group and children (processes.py:79-86); the local path runs no disk scan; the cache write is a uuid temp file plus os.replace, so readers never see a partial file (local.py:462-471); the workspace is a git clone --shared, read-only on the object store; reviewer HOMEs are fresh per attempt. CI already runs reviews of different PRs concurrently against the same gateway (review job concurrency is per PR) and omp auth-gateway has no concurrency limit. Quota spent is the sum of reviews whatever their order, so serialising delays reviews without saving quota, except when two runs review the same patch: then the second can reuse the first's cached result. The only exclusion the design needs is per cache key.

Outcome: lock on the cache key (cache/<key>.lock); inside the lock re-check the cache, so a duplicate review waits and reuses the result; reviews of different patches run in parallel. The wait cap stays one hour per key.

Decision gates:
1. If any machine-global shared resource is found during implementation that the analysis missed (a file, port, process check or account limit), stop and record it before choosing a scope.

Item guardrails: fail closed unchanged (unavailable, quota and absence still refuse); no change to cache key contents; tests use real flock in two processes, not mocks.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. Never use git stash (refs/stash is shared across worktrees). Commit as Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>, staging explicit paths only; no git add -A, no --no-verify, no SKIP, no agent trailers. Durable text (commits, PR bodies, docs, code) carries no tracker ids, session labels or plan references. Maintained code has no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). Before publishing run make docs-reference-inventory-check, make doc-contracts-guard and make pr-preflight, and self-review with the code review action, fixing every Critical and Required finding. Publish only with make pr-open: never gh pr create, a raw push-and-open, or a PR-body override line; if make pr-open refuses, stop and report the exact refusal instead of routing around it. Until oracle-omp-pin-single-source-20261026 merges, make pr-open may run only with PATH prefixed by the darwin-arm64 omp 18.12.1 build recorded in that item (SHA-256 fa41b27d434380e99b713e4f9ced0f73eb1fc0c409fdf23a57c119971d24bac5, from https://build.stencil.so/d/omp/20261017-231446-291e055/omp-darwin-arm64), verified with shasum immediately before use; never any other side-loaded omp. Close out only with oracle SHIP on the exact head, every oracle thread answered (reply naming the fixing SHA, then resolve) and make pr-arm; never raw gh pr merge or a ruleset or settings change, and never a stand-in, adjudication or backoff reset unless the owner names the PR and head (and the finding) in the current request after an Owner instruction comment.
